messages:
maria: Heads-up — finalizing console changes around per-route analytics + routing hints. Need a quick decision on saved-view scoping: should saved queries let users pin both route + model (variant) together, or keep model selection a separate transient control?

raj: I'd lean combined pin. For infra teams the model choice is critical to reproduce costs & perf.

alex: +1 for reproducibility. Main concern: quota/billing attribution. Right now quotas are keyed by route_id only. If we pin model we need to surface model_id in billing/quotas or we risk surprising customers.

elaine: If we require a backend change that will affect the route-presets API. Can we do a client-side shim for the first rollout that persists the pin in the view but maps to route-level quota until backend is ready?

sam: Also think about sampling: saved views might implicitly change what telemetry is sampled or how cost previews are computed. If we persist model pins, we should persist the sampling hints too (or at least record them).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout started for console-saveview-v3 to staging at 3198765450 :rocket:

alex: Proposal sketch for API change: add optional "model_scope" on view resource. Example: GET /views -> [{ id, name, filters, model_scope: "route_model" | "route_only" | "org_default" }]

maria: I prefer explicit enumerants but with clearer names: "route_model", "route_only", "org_default" works. Let's avoid ambiguous names like "pinned".

raj: Telemetry note: we should record both requested_model_id and effective_model_id in traces (for when fallback routing happens). That'll make regressions/debugging way clearer.

elaine: UX suggestion: in the save modal show a tiny badge that says "model pinned" with hover text: "This view will always request this model for this route; may affect cost and latency." Also add an "Ignore model pin" quick toggle for on-the-fly exploration.

sam: Edge-case: routes that A/B across multiple model variants — the pin must be variant-specific (variant_id) rather than just family name. Otherwise saved view behavior will be inconsistent during multi-model rollouts.

alex: Backend implementation note: cheap path is to keep quota calc keyed by route_id and add model_id as an optional secondary key behind a FF. When enabled, billing metrics will break out by model_id; when disabled, fallback to route-level attribution.

maria: Proposed decision (for this thread): hybrid approach. 1) Do not change existing saved views. 2) New saved views default to route_model pin = opt-in (UI exposes option). 3) Launch model-aware quotas behind a feature flag and migrate customers on request. Rollout plan?

raj: Agree. Migration plan: 2-week opt-in banner in console for existing views -> prompt to "upgrade" to model-aware view. Track acceptance. Also keep old sharing links working.

elaine: I'll draft the banner copy this afternoon. Will ensure link points to migration modal.

sam: Tests: unit for view serialization, e2e for pin/unpin behavior, and a telemetry e2e to verify requested_model_id vs effective_model_id in traces.

maria: Action items: @elaine write banner + modal copy; @alex spec the API + feature flag behavior; @raj add telemetry fields & schema update; @sam write tests + e2e. Who will own rollout checklist (monitoring, cost alerts, rollback plan)?

alex: I'll own the rollout checklist. Starting spec PR now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pull/8123 (WIP).

raj: I'll add telemetry schema change to the infra board and put a small evaluation job to verify sampling rates don't skew after pinning.

maria: Great. If no objections by EOD we'll freeze the UI changes for a staging push tomorrow. :thumbsup:

elaine: quick note — share links must continue to deserialize view objects even if model_scope field is missing. Keep server tolerant.

sam: Also add a small note in release notes about quota visibility changes for early adopters.

alex: ack. I already added a TODO in the PR for release notes and a short migration FAQ.

maria: Thanks all — will follow up with a short doc outlining the rollout timeline & monitoring thresholds.

raj: one more tiny UX ask: in per-route model dropdown, show a subtle cost preview (tokens/minute estimate) when selecting model variants so users understand impact before pinning.

elaine: good call. I'll add that to the mock.

maria: OK wrapping up. If you need to chat real-time about API shape, ping me or set up a 15m.

alex: quick FYI — added a sample GET/POST schema in the PR description.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Staging deploy complete at 3198765500 :white_check_mark:
